description: Detection of PsExec lateral movement and service execution.
human_action: An attempt to remotely execute commands via PsExec was detected. This is a primary method for lateral movement within a domain.
long_description: PsExec works by installing a temporary service (PSEXESVC.exe) on the remote machine via administrative shares (ADMIN$). It then establishes named pipes for communication.
remediation: Isolate the target node (SC-7). Terminate PSEXESVC.exe. Audit for new services (SI-7) and unauthorized admin share access (\ADMIN$).
tactical_intent: Establish remote command execution and escalate to SYSTEM privileges via service installation.
attack_mechanism: PsExec service installation (PSEXESVC) and administrative share abuse.

description: Detection of wuauclt.exe LOLBAS abuse for defense evasion.
human_action: The Windows Update Client (wuauclt.exe) is being used to load a DLL from a suspicious path. This is a known technique to bypass security filters.
long_description: The Windows Update Client (wuauclt.exe) can be abused to load arbitrary DLLs via the /UpdateDeploymentProvider flag, hijacking a legitimate process.
remediation: Isolate host immediately (SC-7). Execute forensic memory capture (AU-12). Revoke all active session tokens for the target node.
tactical_intent: Execute unauthorized arbitrary code/DLLs by hijacking legitimate Windows Update client (Defense Evasion).
attack_mechanism: Windows Update Client (wuauclt.exe) DLL sideloading via /UpdateDeploymentProvider.

description: NIST AC-3: Explicit OS Credential Access
human_action: Someone tried to steal your saved passwords via known offensive tooling (Mimikatz, etc).
long_description: Detection of explicit offensive tooling (Mimikatz, Procdump, etc.) accessing secrets.
remediation: Assume all local and domain credentials cached on this system are compromised. IMMEDIATE DOMAIN PASSWORD RESET REQUIRED.
tactical_intent: Harvest administrative credentials to facilitate domain-wide escalation.
attack_mechanism: Credential extraction from memory or registry.

description: NIST IA-2: LSASS Memory Access / Credential Dumping
human_action: An unauthorized process is attempting to read the memory of LSASS.exe, which contains system passwords.
long_description: Detection of non-standard processes requesting high-privilege access (0x1FFFFF, 0x1010) to the LSASS memory space.
remediation: Immediately isolate the host. Change all local and domain passwords. Review the 'Source Image' to identify the malicious process.
tactical_intent: Harvest administrative credentials from memory to facilitate domain-wide escalation.
attack_mechanism: LSASS memory dumping via toolsets like Mimikatz or Procdump.

description: Detection of audit log clearing or service tampering
human_action: Your security logs were just cleared. This is a high-severity anti-forensic indicator.
long_description: Clearing audit logs or stopping the logging service is a high-severity indicator of anti-forensic activity.
remediation: Investigate why the log service was stopped or cleared. Check for unauthorized administrative access.
tactical_intent: Cover tracks by deleting forensic evidence or disabling monitoring services.
attack_mechanism: Log clearing (wevtutil cl) or service termination (net stop).

human_action: An attempt to export or save the Windows SAM or SECURITY registry hives was detected.
long_description: Detection of 'reg save', 'reg export', or direct file access to sensitive registry hive backups (SAM, SECURITY, SYSTEM).
remediation: Check for suspicious files on the filesystem (e.g., sam.hiv, security.hiv). Isolate the host.
tactical_intent: Exfiltrate local account hashes for offline cracking and privilege escalation.
attack_mechanism: Registry hive exfiltration via 'reg save' or 'reg export'.

description: Proactive detection of signed binary proxy execution (LOLBAS).
human_action: A trusted Windows system file is being used to run unauthorized code or download files.
long_description: Behavioral detection of Microsoft-signed binaries from System32/SysWOW64 interacting with suspicious paths (Temp, AppData, Public, ProgramData).
remediation: Immediately isolate the host. Investigate the process lineage to identify the initial entry point.
adversary_profile: Internal System Process / Native Proxy Execution
tactical_intent: Execute unauthorized arbitrary code while masquerading as a legitimate system process.

human_action: Large amounts of data are being sent from your computer to an unknown location.
long_description: Detection of massive data exfiltration via HTTP POST bodies, characteristic of backdoor C2 beaconing.
remediation: Immediately isolate the host. Extract the 'Host:' header from the forensic evidence to identify the C2/DGA domain.
tactical_intent: Establish Command & Control (C2) channel and exfiltrate sensitive data.

description: Windows Forensic: System Integrity / Active Exploit
human_action: Disconnect your computer from the internet immediately. Run Windows Update and change passwords.
long_description: Detection of system manifest corruption, execution of discovery tools, or highly definitive exploit markers.
remediation: Immediately isolate host and freeze network segment. Run DISM repair.
tactical_intent: Establish persistence and escalate privileges across the internal segment.
attack_mechanism: Generic system exploit or baseline deviation.

description: NIST SI-4: DCSync Replication Attack Detection
human_action: A non-Domain Controller account is attempting to replicate the Active Directory database. This is a high-confidence indicator of the DCSync technique used by Mimikatz to steal domain hashes.
long_description: The DCSync technique abuses the Microsoft Directory Replication Service (DRS) Remote Protocol to impersonate a domain controller and request account data. It requires specific replication permissions (DS-Replication-Get-Changes).
remediation: IMMEDIATE DOMAIN COMPROMISE PROTOCOL. Isolate the source account and node. Reset all administrative passwords. Review replication permissions on the Domain object.
tactical_intent: Steal Active Directory credentials (hashes) without accessing the NTDS.dit file or memory of the LSASS process on a Domain Controller.
attack_mechanism: Directory Replication Service (DRS) GetChanges/GetChangesAll requests from non-DC accounts.
